units.zh: 先主甘皇后
units.en: Lady Gan, consort of Liu Bei (styled the First Lord)
units.literal: Empress Gan of the First Lord

units.zh: 先主甘皇后，沛人也。
units.en: Lady Gan came from Pei.
units.literal: Empress Gan of the First Lord was a native of Pei.

units.zh: 先主臨豫州，住小沛，納以為妾。
units.en: While Liu Bei held Yuzhou and made his base at Xiaopei, he took her as a concubine.
units.literal: When the First Lord came to Yu prefecture and dwelt at Little Pei, he took her in as a concubine.

units.zh: 先主數喪嫡室，常攝內事。
units.en: He had buried several chief wives in succession, so she habitually ran the inner quarters.
units.literal: The First Lord repeatedly lost his principal wives, and she constantly managed affairs within the household.

units.zh: 隨先主於荊州，產後主。
units.en: In Jingzhou she gave birth to the future emperor Liu Shan.
units.literal: She followed the First Lord in Jing province and bore the Later Lord.

units.zh: 值曹公軍至，追及先主於當陽長阪，於時困偪，棄後及後主，賴趙雲保護，得免於難。
units.en: When Cao Cao’s host caught Liu Bei at Changban in Dangyang, the retreat was so desperate that he abandoned Lady Gan and the boy; only Zhao Yun’s shielding brought them through alive.
units.literal: When Lord Cao’s army arrived and overtook the First Lord at Changban Slope in Dangyang, at that time hard pressed, he abandoned the empress and the Later Lord; thanks to Zhao Yun’s protection they escaped the peril.

units.zh: 後卒，葬於南郡。
units.en: She died later and was interred in Nan commandery.
units.literal: Later she died and was buried in Nan commandery.

units.zh: 章武二年，追諡皇思夫人，遷葬於蜀，未至而先主殂隕。
units.en: In Zhangwu 2 she received the posthumous title Lady of Imperial Remembrance and her coffin was ordered west into Shu, but Liu Bei died before the cortège arrived.
units.literal: In the second year of Zhangwu she was posthumously titled Lady of Imperial Remembrance, and her burial was to be moved to Shu, but before it arrived the First Lord passed away.

units.zh: 丞相亮上言：
units.en: Zhuge Liang memorialized as follows:
units.literal: The Chancellor Liang submitted:

units.zh: 皇思夫人履行脩仁，淑慎其身。
units.en: The late Lady of Imperial Remembrance lived with integrity and kindness, modest and guarded in deportment.
units.literal: The Lady of Imperial Remembrance practiced conduct and cultivated benevolence, chaste and careful in her person.

units.zh: 大行皇帝昔在上將，嬪妃作合，載育聖躬，大命不融。
units.en: When our late sovereign was still a field commander, she joined him in wedlock and bore his heir, though heaven cut that union short.
units.literal: The late emperor, in former days as a general, was matched with a consort who bore and nurtured his sacred person, yet the great mandate did not endure.

units.zh: 大行皇帝存時，篤義垂恩，念皇思夫人神柩在遠飄颻，特遣使者奉迎。
units.en: In his lifetime he never forgot her: learning her coffin still wandered far from the capital, he sent envoys to escort it home.
units.literal: While the late emperor lived he was deeply dutiful and showed favor, remembering that the Lady of Imperial Remembrance’s spirit coffin drifted far away, and specially dispatched envoys to welcome it.

units.zh: 會大行皇帝崩，今皇思夫人神柩以到，又梓宮在道，園陵將成，安厝有期。
units.en: He has since died, yet her catafalque has now reached us while his own bier is still en route and the imperial tombs near completion, so both burials may soon be ordered.
units.literal: It happened that the late emperor died; now the Lady of Imperial Remembrance’s spirit coffin has arrived, and moreover the catalpa coffin is on the road, the mausoleum park nearly complete, and the date for laying her to rest is set.

units.zh: 臣輒與太常臣賴恭等議：《禮記》曰：『立愛自親始，教民孝也；
units.en: I have consulted Minister Lai Gong and others. The Book of Rites teaches, 'Teach love by starting with one’s parents—thus the people learn filial piety;
units.literal: Your servant has rashly deliberated with Minister of Ceremonies Lai Gong and others: the Record of Rites says, 'Establish love beginning with kin—this teaches the people filial piety;

units.zh: 立敬自長始，教民順也。』
units.en: teach respect by starting with one’s elders—thus the people learn deference.'
units.literal: establish reverence beginning with elders—this teaches the people obedience.'

units.zh: 不忘其親，所由生也。
units.en: To forget not those who gave you life is the root of all moral feeling.
units.literal: Not forgetting one’s kin is the source from which life proceeds.

units.zh: 春秋之義，母以子貴。
units.en: The Spring and Autumn canon holds that a mother’s rank rises with her son’s.
units.literal: By the principle of the Spring and Autumn Annals, the mother is honored because of her son.

units.zh: 昔高皇帝追尊太上昭靈夫人為昭靈皇后，孝和皇帝改葬其母梁貴人，尊號曰恭懷皇后，孝愍皇帝亦改葬其母王夫人，尊號曰靈懷皇后。
units.en: Gaozu of Han raised his mother to Empress Zhaoling; He-di reinterred Lady Liang as Empress Gonghuai; Min-di did the same for Lady Wang as Empress Linghuai.
units.literal: In antiquity the High Emperor posthumously honored the Grand Supreme Lady Zhao Ling as Empress Zhao Ling; Emperor Xiaohe reburied his mother the Honored Lady Liang with the title Empress Gonghuai; Emperor Xiaomin likewise reburied his mother Lady Wang with the title Empress Linghuai.

units.zh: 今皇思夫人宜有尊號，以慰寒泉之思，輒與恭等案諡法，宜曰昭烈皇后。
units.en: She therefore deserves a throne name that may comfort the living. We have weighed the statutes of posthumous honor and propose Empress Zhaolie.
units.literal: Now the Lady of Imperial Remembrance ought to receive an exalted title to console thoughts from the cold spring; your servant has rashly with Gong and others examined the posthumous-title code—she should be called Empress Zhaolie.

units.zh: 詩曰：『谷則異室，死則同穴。』
units.en: The Classic of Poetry says, ‘We dwelt apart in life; we lie together in death.’
units.literal: The Odes say, ‘In life we dwelt in different chambers; in death we share one grave.’

units.zh: 〈《禮》云：上古無合葬，中古後因時方有。〉
units.en: Commentary: The Rites note that joint burial was unknown in earliest ages and became practice only in later ages.〉
units.literal: 〈The Rites states: In high antiquity there was no joint burial; from middle antiquity onward it arose with the times.〉

units.zh: 故昭烈皇后宜與大行皇帝合葬，臣請太尉告宗廟，布露天下，具禮儀別奏。
units.en: We therefore ask that she be laid beside the late emperor, that the grand commandant report this to the shrines of state, that an edict proclaim it to the realm, and that the detailed rites be submitted in a further memorial.
units.literal: Therefore Empress Zhaolie ought to be buried with the late emperor; your servant requests the Grand Commandant announce this in the ancestral temples, publish it throughout the realm, and separately memorialize the full ritual observances.

units.zh: 制曰可。
units.en: The sovereign’s reply read: Granted.
units.literal: The rescript said: Approved.

units.zh: 先主穆皇后，陳留人也。
units.en: Lady Mu, empress of Liu Bei, came from Chenliu.
units.literal: Empress Mu of the First Lord was a native of Chenliu.

units.zh: 兄吳壹，少孤，壹父素與劉焉有舊，是以舉家隨焉入蜀。
units.en: Her brother Wu Yi was orphaned young. Their father had been close to Liu Yan, so the whole family followed Yan into Shu.
units.literal: Her elder brother was Wu Yi; orphaned young, Yi's father had long been on familiar terms with Liu Yan, and on that account the whole family followed Yan into Shu.

units.zh: 焉有異志，而聞善相者相后當大貴。
units.en: Liu Yan nurtured separate ambitions, and word came that a physiognomist had foretold the girl would rise to great rank.
units.literal: Yan harbored separate ambitions, and it was heard that a skilled physiognomist predicted the empress would attain great honor.

units.zh: 焉時將子瑁自隨，遂為瑁納后。
units.en: Liu Yan then had his son Mao marry her.
units.literal: At the time Yan took his son Mao with him; thereupon he had Mao take the empress in marriage.

units.zh: 瑁死，后寡居。
units.en: When Mao died she remained a widow.
units.literal: Mao died; the empress lived in widowhood.

units.zh: 先主既定益州，而孫夫人還吳，《漢晉春秋》云：先主入益州，吳遣迎孫夫人。
units.en: Once Liu Bei held Yizhou, Lady Sun went back to Wu. The Spring and Autumn of Han and Jin says Wu sent to fetch her when Liu Bei entered Yizhou.
units.literal: After the First Lord had settled Yizhou, Lady Sun returned to Wu. The Spring and Autumn of Han and Jin states: When the First Lord entered Yizhou, Wu sent to welcome Lady Sun.

units.zh: 夫人欲將太子歸吳，諸葛亮使趙雲勒兵斷江留太子，乃得止。
units.en: She meant to take the crown prince with her, but Zhuge Liang had Zhao Yun seal the river and keep the boy—only then was she stopped.
units.literal: The lady wished to take the crown prince back to Wu; Zhuge Liang had Zhao Yun draw up troops and block the river to keep the crown prince—only then was it stopped.

units.zh: 群下勸先主聘后，先主疑與瑁同族，法正進曰：「論其親疏，何與晉文之於子圉乎？」
units.en: His court urged Liu Bei to wed her, but he worried she was kin to Mao. Fa Zheng argued: "By closeness of kin, how does this resemble Duke Wen of Jin and Zi Yu?"
units.literal: The assembly urged the First Lord to take the empress as bride; the First Lord suspected she was of the same clan as Mao. Fa Zheng advanced and said, "As to degrees of kinship, how does this compare with Duke Wen of Jin and Zi Yu?"

units.zh: 於是納后為夫人。
units.en: He then took her as consort.
units.literal: Thereupon he took the empress in as his lady.

units.zh: 習鑿齒曰：夫婚姻，人倫之始，王化之本，匹夫猶不可以無禮，而況人君乎？
units.en: Xi Zaochi wrote: Marriage begins human order and grounds royal civilizing rule; even commoners must observe ritual—how much more a sovereign?
units.literal: Xi Zaochi said: Marriage is the beginning of human relations and the root of royal transformation; even common men cannot lack ritual—how much more a ruler?

units.zh: 晉文廢禮行權，以濟其業，故子犯曰，有求於人，必先從之，將奪其國，何有於妻，非無故而違禮教者也。
units.en: Duke Wen of Jin set ritual aside and used expedient power to save his cause; hence Zi Fan said that when one needs others one must first yield, and when one is about to seize a state what care is there for a wife?—that was not capricious breach of ritual.
units.literal: Duke Wen of Jin set ritual aside and exercised expedient power to save his enterprise; hence Zi Fan said: when one has need of others, one must first yield to them; about to seize their state, what care for a wife?—this was not violating ritual teaching without cause.

units.zh: 今先主無權事之偪，而引前失以為譬，非導其君以堯、舜之道者。
units.en: Liu Bei faced no such coercion, yet Fa Zheng cited an old lapse as precedent—this was not guiding a ruler along the path of Yao and Shun.
units.literal: Now the First Lord had no coercion of expedient affairs, yet cited a past fault as precedent—this is not guiding one's lord by the Way of Yao and Shun.

units.zh: 先主從之，過矣。
units.en: Liu Bei took the advice—a mistake, in Xi Zaochi's view.
units.literal: The First Lord followed it—an error.

units.zh: 建安二十四年，立為漢中王后。
units.en: In Jian'an 24 she was made queen of Hanzhong.
units.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Jian'an she was established as queen of Hanzhong.

units.zh: 章武元年夏五月，策曰：「朕承天命，奉至尊，臨萬國。
units.en: In the fifth month of Zhangwu 1 an edict ran: "I receive Heaven's mandate, hold supreme dignity, and rule the myriad states.
units.literal: In the fifth month of summer in the first year of Zhangwu the patent read, "We receive Heaven's mandate, hold the supreme dignity, and face the myriad states.

units.zh: 今以后為皇后，遣使持節丞相亮授璽綬，承宗廟，母天下，皇后其敬之哉！」
units.en: I now make the empress queen, send envoys with the imperial baton for Chancellor Zhuge Liang to confer her seals and cords, that she may receive the ancestral shrines and mother the realm—revere this charge, O empress!"
units.literal: Now We make the empress queen, dispatch envoys bearing the tally for Chancellor Liang to confer seals and ribbons, to receive the ancestral temples and mother the realm—may the empress revere this charge!"

units.zh: 建興元年223年五月，後主即位，尊后為皇太后，稱長樂宮。
units.en: In the fifth month of Jianxing 1 (223 CE) Liu Shan succeeded and raised her to empress dowager of Changle Palace.
units.literal: In the fifth month of the first year of Jianxing (223 CE) the Later Lord ascended the throne and honored the empress as empress dowager, with her residence called Changle Palace.

units.zh: 壹官至車騎將軍，封縣侯。
units.en: Wu Yi rose to general of chariots and cavalry and received a district marquisate.
units.literal: Yi rose to General of Chariots and Cavalry and was enfeoffed as a district marquis.

units.zh: 延熙八年，后薨，合葬惠陵。
units.en: In Yanxi 8 she died and was interred with Liu Bei at Huiling.
units.literal: In the eighth year of Yanxi the empress died and was buried with the First Lord at Huiling.

units.zh: 孫盛《蜀世譜》曰：壹孫喬，沒李雄中三十年，不為雄屈也。
units.en: Sun Sheng's Shu genealogy notes that Wu Yi's grandson Qiao, held among Li Xiong's forces for thirty years, never bowed to Xiong.
units.literal: Sun Sheng's Genealogy of Shu states: Yi's grandson Qiao, captured among Li Xiong's forces for thirty years, would not submit to Xiong.

units.zh: 後主敬哀皇后，車騎將軍張飛長女也。
units.en: Liu Shan’s Empress Jing’ai was the eldest daughter of Zhang Fei, general of chariots and cavalry.
units.literal: Empress Jing’ai of the Later Lord was the eldest daughter of General of Chariots and Cavalry Zhang Fei.

units.zh: 章武元年，納為太子妃。
units.en: In Zhangwu 1 she entered the palace as crown princess.
units.literal: In the first year of Zhangwu she was taken in as heir’s consort.

units.zh: 建興元年，立為皇后。
units.en: Jianxing 1 saw her enthroned as empress.
units.literal: In the first year of Jianxing she was established as empress.

units.zh: 十五年薨，葬南陵。
units.en: She died in the fifteenth Jianxing year and was buried at Nanling.
units.literal: In the fifteenth year she died and was buried at Nan Mausoleum.

units.zh: 後主張皇后，前后敬哀之妹也。
units.en: Liu Shan's Empress Zhang was the younger sister of Empress Jing'ai.
units.literal: Empress Zhang of the Later Lord was the younger sister of the former Empress Jing'ai.

units.zh: 建興十五年237年，入為貴人。
units.en: In Jianxing 15 (237 CE) she entered the palace as an honored lady.
units.literal: In the fifteenth year of Jianxing (237 CE) she entered the palace as an honored lady.

units.zh: 延熙元年238年春正月，策曰：「朕統承大業，君臨天下，奉郊廟社稷。
units.en: In the first month of Yanxi 1 (238 CE) an edict ran: "I inherit the great enterprise, rule the realm, and serve the suburban altars and state shrines.
units.literal: In the first month of spring in the first year of Yanxi (238 CE) the patent read, "We inherit the great enterprise, face the realm, and serve the suburban altars and state shrines.

units.zh: 今以貴人為皇后，使行丞相事左將軍向朗持節授璽綬。
units.en: I now make the honored lady empress and dispatch Xiang Lang, left general acting as chancellor, with the imperial baton to present her seals and cords.
units.literal: Now We make the honored lady empress, and order Xiang Lang, left general acting as chancellor, to bear the tally and confer seals and ribbons.

units.zh: 勉脩中饋，恪肅禋祀，皇后其敬之哉！」
units.en: Cultivate the inner household and reverently keep the state sacrifices—revere this charge, O empress!"
units.literal: Strive to cultivate inner household duties and reverently keep sacrificial rites—may the empress revere this charge!"

units.zh: 咸熙元年，隨後主遷於洛陽。
units.en: In Xianxi 1 she followed Liu Shan to Luoyang.
units.literal: In the first year of Xianxi she followed the Later Lord in removal to Luoyang.

units.zh: 《漢晉春秋》曰：魏以蜀宮人賜諸將之無妻者，李昭儀曰：「我不能二三屈辱。」
units.en: The Spring and Autumn of Han and Jin says Wei gave Shu palace women to generals without wives. Lady Li, the Zhaoyi, said, "I cannot endure repeated humiliation."
units.literal: The Spring and Autumn of Han and Jin states: Wei gave Shu palace women to generals without wives; Lady Li the Zhaoyi said, "I cannot endure repeated humiliation."

units.zh: 乃自殺。
units.en: She then took her own life.
units.literal: Thereupon she killed herself.

units.zh: 劉永字公壽，先主子，後主庶弟也。
units.en: Liu Yong, styled Gongshou, was Liu Bei's son and Liu Shan's younger half-brother.
units.literal: Liu Yong, courtesy Gongshou, was a son of the First Lord and a younger half-brother of the Later Lord.

units.zh: 章武元年六月，使司徒靖立永為魯王，策曰：「小子永，受茲青土。
units.en: In the sixth month of Zhangwu 1 Liu Bei ordered Xu Jing, minister of education, to enfeoff Liu Yong as prince of Lu. The edict ran: "Young Liu Yong, receive this azure soil.
units.literal: In the sixth month of the first year of Zhangwu the emperor ordered Minister of Education Xu Jing to invest Yong as Prince of Lu; the patent read, "Young Yong, receive this azure soil.

units.zh: 朕承天序，繼統大業，遵脩稽古，建爾國家，封於東土，奄有龜蒙，世為籓輔。
units.en: I carry on Heaven's line, continue the great enterprise, observe antiquity, establish your state, enfeoff you in the east, embrace Gui and Meng, and make you a feudal shield for generations.
units.literal: We inherit Heaven's sequence, continue the great enterprise, observe and restore antiquity, establish your state and house, enfeoff you in the eastern lands, embrace Gui and Meng, and make you a feudal bulwark for generations.

units.zh: 嗚呼，恭朕之詔！
units.en: Revere this charge of mine!
units.literal: Alas, revere Our edict!

units.zh: 惟彼魯邦，一變適道，風化存焉。
units.en: Lu, once transformed, was fit for the Way; civilizing rule endures there.
units.literal: That state of Lu, once transformed, was fit for the Way; civilizing transformation abides there.

units.zh: 人之好德，世茲懿美。
units.en: Its people's love of virtue is a lasting excellence.
units.literal: Men's love of virtue there is ever this excellent beauty.

units.zh: 王其秉心率禮，綏爾士民，是饗是宜，其戒之哉！」
units.en: Hold your heart to ritual, pacify your officers and people, receive what is fitting—revere this charge, my prince!"
units.literal: May you, my prince, hold your heart and lead by ritual, pacify your officers and people, receive and keep what is fitting—revere this charge!"

units.zh: 建興八年230年，改封為甘陵王。
units.en: In Jianxing 8 (230 CE) his title was changed to prince of Ganling.
units.literal: In the eighth year of Jianxing (230 CE) his fief was changed to Prince of Ganling.

units.zh: 初，永憎宦人黃皓，皓既信任用事，譖構永於後主，後主稍疏外永，至不得朝見者十餘年。
units.en: Liu Yong hated the eunuch Huang Hao. Once Huang Hao gained power he slandered Liu Yong to Liu Shan, who gradually kept him at arm's length until for more than ten years he could not attend court.
units.literal: At first Yong detested the eunuch Huang Hao; once Hao gained trust and wielded power he slandered Yong to the Later Lord, and the Later Lord gradually kept Yong at a distance until for more than ten years he could not attend court audiences.

units.zh: 咸熙元年，永東遷洛陽，拜奉車都尉，封為鄉侯。
units.en: In Xianxi 1 Liu Yong went east to Luoyang, became commandant of the imperial carriage, and received a village marquisate.
units.literal: In the first year of Xianxi Yong moved east to Luoyang, was appointed Commandant of the Imperial Carriage, and enfeoffed as a village marquis.

units.zh: 劉理字奉孝，亦後主庶弟也，與永異母。
units.en: Liu Li, styled Fengxiao, was another younger half-brother of Liu Shan, not born to the same mother as Liu Yong.
units.literal: Liu Li, courtesy Fengxiao, was also a younger half-brother of the Later Lord by a different mother from Yong.

units.zh: 章武元年六月，使司徒靖立理為梁王，策曰：「小子理，朕統承漢序，祗順天命，遵脩典秩，建爾於東，為漢籓輔。
units.en: In the sixth month of Zhangwu 1 Liu Bei ordered Xu Jing, minister of education, to enfeoff Liu Li as prince of Liang. The edict ran: “Young Liu Li, I carry on Han’s line, bow to heaven’s charge, and uphold the statutes; I therefore enfeoff you in the east as a feudal shield of the house of Han.
units.literal: In the sixth month of the first year of Zhangwu the emperor ordered Minister of Education Xu Jing to invest Li as Prince of Liang; the patent read, "Young Li, We inherit the sequence of Han, reverently obey Heaven’s mandate, observe canonical order, and establish you in the east as a feudal bulwark of Han.

units.zh: 惟彼梁土，畿甸之邦，民狎教化，易導以禮。
units.en: Liang lies within the royal domain; its people are used to civilizing rule and readily led by ritual.
units.literal: That land of Liang is a domain within the capital region; the people are intimate with instruction and easily guided by ritual.

units.zh: 往悉乃心，懷保黎庶，以永爾國，王其敬之哉！」
units.en: Go with a whole heart, shelter the common folk, and so long preserve your state—revere this charge, my prince!”
units.literal: Go forth with all your heart, cherish and protect the black-haired masses, and thereby perpetuate your state—may you, my prince, revere these words!"

units.zh: 建興八年，改封理為安平王。
units.en: In Jianxing 8 his title was changed to prince of Anping.
units.literal: In the eighth year of Jianxing Li’s fief was changed to Prince of Anping.

units.zh: 延熙七年卒，諡曰悼王。
units.en: He died in Yanxi 7 and received the posthumous epithet Prince Dao (Lamented).
units.literal: In the seventh year of Yanxi he died; his posthumous title was Prince Dao.

units.zh: 子哀王胤嗣，十九年卒。
units.en: His son Yin, prince Ai, succeeded and died in the nineteenth year.
units.literal: His son Prince Ai Yin succeeded; in the nineteenth year he died.

units.zh: 子殤王承嗣，二十年卒。
units.en: Cheng, prince Shang, followed and died in the twentieth year.
units.literal: His son Prince Shang Cheng succeeded; in the twentieth year he died.

units.zh: 景耀四年詔曰：「安平王，先帝所命。
units.en: Jingyao 4 brought an edict: “The prince of Anping was enfeoffed by the late sovereign.
units.literal: In the fourth year of Jingyao an edict said, "The Prince of Anping was enfeoffed by the late emperor.

units.zh: 三世早夭，國嗣頹絕，朕用傷悼。
units.en: Three heirs in a row have perished young, leaving the fief without an heir, and We mourn that break.
units.literal: Three generations have died young in succession, and the line of succession has broken off; We are thereby grieved.

units.zh: 其以武邑侯輯襲王位。」
units.en: We therefore order Ji, marquis of Wuyi, to inherit the princedom.”
units.literal: Let Marquis of Wuyi Ji succeed to the princedom."

units.zh: 輯，理子也，咸熙元年，東遷洛陽，拜奉車都尉，封鄉侯。
units.en: Ji was Liu Li’s son. In Xianxi 1 he went east to Luoyang, became commandant of the imperial carriage, and received a village marquisate.
units.literal: Ji was Li’s son; in the first year of Xianxi he moved east to Luoyang, was appointed Commandant of the Imperial Carriage, and enfeoffed as village marquis.

units.zh: 後主太子 璿
units.en: Liu Xuan, crown prince of Liu Shan
units.literal: Crown Prince Xuan of the Later Lord

units.zh: 後主太子璿，字文衡。
units.en: Liu Xuan, styled Wenheng, was Liu Shan’s heir apparent.
units.literal: Crown Prince Xuan of the Later Lord, courtesy Wenheng.

units.zh: 母王貴人，本敬哀張皇后侍人也。
units.en: His mother was Lady Wang, once a maid to Empress Jing’ai of the Zhang clan.
units.literal: His mother was Honored Lady Wang, originally a handmaid of Empress Jing’ai née Zhang.

units.zh: 延熙元年正月策曰：「在昔帝王，繼體立嗣，副貳國統，古今常道。
units.en: Yanxi 1 opened with an edict: “Since antiquity sovereigns have named heirs to carry on the flesh and serve as second to the throne—
units.literal: In the first month of the first year of Yanxi the patent said, "Of old emperors and kings, continuing the body and establishing the heir, appointing a deputy for the state’s succession, has been the constant way from ancient to present.

units.zh: 今以璿為皇太子，昭顯祖宗之威，命使行丞相事左將軍朗持節授印緩。
units.en: We therefore invest Liu Xuan as crown prince so the ancestors’ awe may shine abroad, and We dispatch Lang, left general acting as chancellor, with the imperial baton to present his seals and cords.
units.literal: Now We make Xuan crown prince, to manifest the majesty of the ancestors; We order Lang, acting as chancellor and general of the left, to bear the tally and confer seals and ribbons.

units.zh: 其勉脩茂質，祗恪道義，諮詢典禮，敬友師傅，斟酌眾善，翼成爾德，可不務脩以自勗哉！」
units.en: Cultivate excellence in yourself, hold fast to duty and the moral law, study the rites, honor your teachers, sift good counsel from many voices, and so grow into virtue—how could you not strive to improve and press yourself forward?”
units.literal: Strive to cultivate a rich nature, reverently keep to the Way and its duties, consult the canons of ritual, respectfully befriend your tutors, weigh the counsel of many good men, and thereby wing your virtue—can you fail to labor at cultivation and urge yourself onward!"

units.zh: 時年十五。
units.en: He was fifteen sui at the time.
units.literal: At that time he was fifteen.

units.zh: 景耀六年冬，蜀亡。
units.en: In the winter of Jingyao 6 the state of Shu was extinguished.
units.literal: In the winter of the sixth year of Jingyao Shu fell.

units.zh: 咸熙元年正月，鍾會作亂於成都，璿為亂兵所害。
units.en: In the first month of Xianxi 1 Zhong Hui mutinied at Chengdu, and Liu Xuan was cut down by the riotous soldiery.
units.literal: In the first month of the first year of Xianxi Zhong Hui raised rebellion in Chengdu, and Xuan was killed by mutinous troops.

units.zh: 〈孫盛《蜀世譜》曰：璿弟，瑤、琮、瓚、諶、恂、璩六人。
units.en: 〈Sun Sheng’s Shu genealogy lists six younger brothers: Yao, Cong, Zan, Chen, Xun, and Qu.
units.literal: 〈Sun Sheng’s Genealogy of Shu states: Xuan had younger brothers Yao, Cong, Zan, Chen, Xun, and Qu—six men.

units.zh: 蜀敗，諶自殺，餘皆內徙。
units.en: When Shu collapsed Chen took his own life; the others were deported to the interior.
units.literal: When Shu fell, Chen committed suicide; the rest were moved inward.

units.zh: 值永嘉大亂，子孫絕滅。
units.en: The Yongjia upheavals wiped out their posterity.
units.literal: They encountered the great turmoil of Yongjia, and descendants were cut off.

units.zh: 唯永孫玄奔蜀，李雄偽署安樂公以嗣禪後。
units.en: Only Liu Yong’s grandson Liu Xuan escaped back into Shu, where Li Xiong named him duke of Anle in mock succession to Liu Shan.
units.literal: Only Yong’s grandson Xuan fled to Shu, and Li Xiong falsely installed him as duke of Anle to continue the line after Shan.

units.zh: 永和三年討李勢，盛參戎行，見玄於成都也。〉
units.en: In Yonghe 3, during the expedition against Li Shi, Sun Sheng himself saw Liu Xuan in Chengdu.〉
units.literal: In the third year of Yonghe, when Li Shi was campaigned against, Sheng took part in the army and saw Xuan at Chengdu.〉

units.en: Commentary
units.literal: 【Commentary】

units.zh: 評曰：易稱有夫婦然後有父子，夫人倫之始，恩紀之隆，莫尚於此矣。
units.en: The historian remarks: The Book of Changes places husband and wife before father and son; no bond in the human order runs deeper or begins earlier.
units.literal: The appraisal states: The Changes says that husband and wife come first, then father and son; nowhere in the beginnings of human relations or the depth of affection and duty is anything higher than this.

units.zh: 是故紀錄，以究一國之體焉。
units.en: They are set down in this chapter so the reader may grasp how one kingdom ordered its inner house.
units.literal: Therefore they are recorded here, to exhaust the pattern of a single state.

units.zh: 習鑿齒曰：昔齊桓一矜其功而叛者九國，曹操暫自驕伐而天下三分，皆勤之於數十年之內而棄之於俯仰之頃，豈不惜乎！
units.en: Xi Zuochi comments: Duke Huan’s single burst of vanity cost him nine allies; Cao Cao’s moment of swagger cost him the unity of the empire. Decades of toil undone in an instant—could anything be more wasteful?
units.literal: Xi Zuochi said: in the past Duke Huan of Qi once prided himself on his merit and nine states rebelled; Cao Cao for a short time was arrogant and boastful and the realm split into three parts; all were toiled over within several tens of years and discarded in the space of a nod and a blink—how is it not regrettable!

units.zh: 璋皆然之，遣法正連好先主，尋又令正及孟達送兵數千助先主守禦，正遂還。
units.en: Liu Zhang agreed, sent Fa Zheng to treat with Liu Bei, and shortly had Fa Zheng and Meng Da deliver several thousand soldiers to stiffen Liu Bei’s line. Fa Zheng then came home.
units.literal: Zhang all approved it; he sent Fa Zheng to connect friendship with the Former Lord; soon he also ordered Zheng and Meng Da to deliver several thousand troops to aid the Former Lord in guarding and defending; Zheng then returned.

units.zh: 璋主簿黃權陳其利害，從事廣漢王累自倒縣於州門以諫，璋一無所納，敕在所供奉先主，先主入境如歸。
units.en: Registrar Huang Quan laid out the risks; Wang Lei of Guanghan hanged himself upside down at the gate of the yamen in protest. Liu Zhang brushed every warning aside, ordered the route provisioned, and Liu Bei crossed the border as though coming home.
units.literal: Zhang’s registrar Huang Quan set forth its benefits and harms; clerk Wang Lei of Guanghan hung himself inverted at the province gate to remonstrate; Zhang accepted none of it; he ordered the places passed through to supply the Former Lord; the Former Lord entered the territory as if returning home.

units.zh: 璋又從之，遣法正請先主。
units.en: Liu Zhang consented again and sent Fa Zheng to invite Liu Bei in.
units.literal: Zhang again followed it; he sent Fa Zheng to invite the Former Lord.

units.zh: 居陽城山，積學教授，舉賢良方正，闢司徒府，歷雒陽令、冀州刺史、南陽太守、宗正、太常。
units.en: He withdrew to Mount Yangcheng, where he studied deeply and taught. Recommended as a worthy and upright candidate, he entered the minister of education’s bureau and rose through Luoyang magistrate, inspector of Ji, grand administrator of Nanyang, director of the imperial clan, and grand master of ceremonies.
units.literal: He dwelt on Mount Yangcheng, amassed learning and taught students; he was recommended as worthy and good, upright and true; he was summoned to the Minister of Education’s office, and in succession served as magistrate of Luoyang, inspector of Ji Province, grand administrator of Nanyang, director of the imperial clan, and grand master of ceremonies.

units.zh: 永康元年167年，日有蝕之，詔舉賢良方正之士，策問得失。
units.en: In 167, the first year of Yongkang, a solar eclipse prompted an edict summoning worthy and upright candidates for written policy examinations.
units.literal: In the first year of Yongkang, 167, there was a solar eclipse; an edict summoned worthy and upright candidates, and policy questions were put on gains and losses.

units.zh: 前後宰府十闢，公車三徵，再舉賢良方正、博士、有道皆不就，名稱尤重。
units.en: Provincial and central offices summoned him ten times, the imperial carriage three times, and he was twice recommended as worthy, erudite, and virtuous—yet he refused every call, and his fame only grew.
units.literal: Before and after, ten summonses came from chief ministers’ offices, three imperial carriage summonses, and twice he was recommended as worthy and upright, as erudite, and as possessing the Way—he accepted none; his reputation was especially weighty.

units.zh: 三年秋九月，追諡故將軍關羽、張飛、馬超、龐統、黃忠。
units.en: That ninth month of 260 posthumous honors were conferred on Guan Yu, Zhang Fei, Ma Chao, Pang Tong, and Huang Zhong.
units.literal: In the autumn, ninth month, of the third year, posthumous titles were granted to the former generals Guan Yu, Zhang Fei, Ma Chao, Pang Tong, and Huang Zhong.

units.zh: 二年夏六月，立子諶為北地王，恂為新興王，虔為上黨王。
units.en: In the sixth month of 259 he enfeoffed Liu Chen as prince of Beidi, Liu Xun as prince of Xinxing, and Liu Qian as prince of Shangdang.
units.literal: In the summer, sixth month, of the second year, his son Chen was established as Prince of Beidi, Xun as Prince of Xinxing, and Qian as Prince of Shangdang.

units.zh: 元康曰：「嘗讀《崔琰傳》，追恨魏武不弘。
units.en: Yuankang said, "I once read the biography of Cui Yan and regretted that Wei Wu was not magnanimous.
units.literal: Yuankang said: "I once read the biography of Cui Yan and regretted that Wei Wu was not magnanimous.

units.zh: 〈孙盛曰：夫玄览未然，逆鉴来事，虽裨灶、梓慎其犹病诸，况术之下此者乎？
units.en: 〈Sun Sheng notes even canonical astrologers stumbled—lesser tricks merit doubt.
units.literal: 〈Sun Sheng said: To survey the unseen and mirror coming events—even Pi Zao and Zi Shen struggled—how much more arts beneath theirs?

units.zh: 吴史书达知东南当有王气，故轻举济江。
units.en: Wu records say Zhao Da crossed south chasing imperial vapors.
units.literal: The Wu history says Da knew kingly qi would rise in the southeast—therefore he lightly crossed the Yangzi.

units.zh: 流俗好异，妄设神奇，不幸之中，仲尼所弃，是以君子志其大者，无所取诸。
units.en: Fashion craves miracles—Confucius spurned fortune-telling—the gentleman thinks bigger.
units.literal: Common fashion loves the strange and vainly fabricates marvels—among ill omens Confucius discarded these—therefore the gentleman sets his aim on greatness and takes nothing from such.

units.zh: 魏承汉绪，受命中畿，达不能豫睹兆萌，而流窜吴越。
units.en: Wei held the Central Plain—yet Zhao Da missed Wei’s rise and wandered eastern marshes.
units.literal: Wei inherited Han’s thread and received mandate in the heartland—Da failed to foresee the budding sign beforehand and drifted among Wu and Yue.

units.zh: 又不知吝术之鄙，见薄於时，安在其能逆睹天道而审帝王之符瑞哉？
units.en: Sun Sheng asks how a stingy technician could read dynastic fate.
units.literal: Again ignorant how base it is to hoard arts—slighted by the age—where lies ability to foresee Heaven’s way and discern imperial portents?

units.zh: 臣松之以为盛云“君子志其大者，无所取诸”，故评家之旨，非新声也。
units.en: Pei Songzhi notes Sun Sheng echoes the official appraisal.
units.literal: Pei Songzhi considers: When Sheng says “the gentleman aims at greatness and takes nothing from such”—the appraiser’s meaning is no novelty.

units.zh: 其餘所讥，则皆为非理。
units.en: Pei rejects Sun Sheng’s other barbs.
units.literal: His remaining ridicule is altogether unreasonable.

units.zh: 因遣使者招永、衍，永、衍等疑不肯降，而忿邑背前約，衍乃遺邑書曰：蓋聞晉文出奔而子犯宣其忠，趙武逢難而程嬰明其賢，二子之義當矣。
units.en: He then sent envoys to summon Bao Yong and Feng Yan; they hesitated and refused to submit, and resenting Tian Yi for breaking their earlier pact, Feng Yan wrote to him: "When Duke Wen of Jin fled into exile, Zi Fan showed his loyalty; when Duke Wu of Zhao met disaster, Cheng Ying proved his worth—both acted as righteousness required."
units.literal: He then sent envoys to summon Yong and Yan; Yong, Yan, and the others, doubting, refused to submit, and resenting Yi for breaking their former pact, Yan sent Yi a letter saying: "I have heard that when Duke Wen of Jin went into exile, Zi Fan proclaimed his loyalty, and when Duke Wu of Zhao met calamity, Cheng Ying made clear his worth—the righteousness of both men was fitting."
